identity.name: Mem0
identity.one_liner: Open-source memory layer for AI agents and assistants that need personalized recall.
identity.short_description: Mem0 is an open-source memory layer for AI applications, designed to store, retrieve, and update user or agent memories across conversations and workflows.

positioning.why_it_matters: Mem0 matters because personalization and continuity are hard to build from scratch. A dedicated memory layer gives agents a place to store durable user facts, preferences, and task history.
best_for: Builders adding long-term memory to agents or chat apps

not_for: Users who want a fully managed consumer product with no setup work
Teams that cannot review the linked source, license, and operational requirements before adoption

seo_article.intro: Mem0 is an open-source memory layer for AI applications, designed to store, retrieve, and update user or agent memories across conversations and workflows.
seo_article.what_it_is: Mem0 is an open memory-system resource to evaluate by what it stores, how recall works, how memory is scoped, and whether users or teams can inspect, correct, export, or delete durable context.
seo_article.why_it_matters: Mem0 matters because personalization and continuity are hard to build from scratch. A dedicated memory layer gives agents a place to store durable user facts, preferences, and task history.
seo_article.how_it_works: Test Mem0 with repeated sessions. Add facts, update them, ask for recall, inspect retrieval behavior, and verify deletion or scoping controls before storing sensitive user or project memory.

faq.question: What should I check before using Mem0?
faq.answer: Test Mem0 with repeated sessions. Add facts, update them, ask for recall, inspect retrieval behavior, and verify deletion or scoping controls before storing sensitive user or project memory.
